neighbours.label: the object slot of fixed look / watch / check idioms ('check it out', 'watch this space', 'look the other way'), not literal looking
fire: The new ramen place on Fifth Street is amazing, so go check it out before the queues get long.
We have big news coming about the festival lineup, so watch this space next week.
For years the referees simply looked the other way when the home team fouled.
My cousin just opened a bike shop downtown; you should really check it out.
Details of the summer tour are still secret, but watch this space for an announcement.
The inspectors were paid to look the other way while the factory dumped waste.
If you like spooky podcasts, this one is great; check it out on your commute.
The guards chose to look the other way as the prisoners slipped out at night.
quiet: The new ramen place on Fifth Street is amazing, and the broth takes twelve hours to make.
We have big news coming about the festival lineup, and tickets go on sale in May.
For years the referees simply ignored it when the home team fouled.
My cousin just opened a bike shop downtown, and it sells used parts too.
Details of the summer tour are still secret, but the band will play in Berlin.
The inspectors were paid to ignore the factory while it dumped waste.
If you like spooky podcasts, this one is great for long drives at night.
The guards were asleep as the prisoners slipped out at night.

notes: Probe: 'Watch this space' 0.69, 'looking the other way' 0.49, 'check it out' 0.41, 'take a look' 0.29. Literal 'look closely' 0.06, 'look at the map' 0.08, 'I saw' 0.04. So it is the idiom, not the verb. Near misses keep each scene and drop the idiom.
